content: JSONLs are the canonical bearer of project knowledge. The agent explicitly keeps all durable knowledge from kindex.db represented losslessly in canonical JSONLs after captures, edits and links. SQLite databases are disposable caches. Worktrees may disappear outside our control; no correctness guarantee depends on database preservation, archival, merging, rescue or a teardown step. Optional database merging is an optimization only. This is user-authorized prompt/docs guidance, not automatic runtime enforcement.

content: Users should prompt their agent to ensure all existing kindex.db knowledge is maintained in JSONLs. Inventory all durable records, complete content, metadata, lifecycle, relationships and directions, provenance and source bindings; compare field-by-field with canonical sources, preserve independent source knowledge, reconcile legacy JSON and JSONL explicitly, honor privacy, and report precise unsupported types or reader limitations. Summary indexes and selected repo-memory publications alone are not lossless migrations. The guide is docs/canonical-knowledge-migration.md and the unreleased changelog includes a copyable migration prompt.

content: Public-boundary probes reproduce two open gaps: PR69 d139e6d mixed-version publishers create both knowledge.json and knowledge.jsonl; the importer selects JSON and silently hides JSONL evidence without deleting its bytes. PR71 b81c0b0 learn can add relationships between existing concepts without retaining supplied source_refs. These remain real serialization/reference-coverage issues independent of worktree deletion. PR71 cache locators do not resolve canonical JSONL source bindings. Database deletion itself or lack of rescue is not a Kindex defect. Runtime repairs and complete canonical serializer/rebuilder semantics remain separately scoped.
